latest_release.name: OpenUsage 0.8.0
latest_release.body:
## v0.8.0

> ## ⚠️ Upgrading From 0.7.x: Read This First
>
> **This is a new OpenUsage. You have to add your accounts again.** Open the **Accounts** screen and sign in to each one. OpenUsage no longer picks up the sign-ins of the coding tools on your Mac, so most accounts don't carry over.
>
> **What carries over**
> - The OpenRouter and Z.ai keys you saved in 0.7.x are added for you, unless you had turned that provider off.
> - Your hidden metrics, metric order, and provider order apply to the first account you add for each provider.
>
> **What is gone**
> - Spend and token estimates from local logs and model pricing. The app shows only what each provider's API reports for the accounts you sign in to.
> - Account discovery. OpenUsage no longer reads other tools' credentials, config files, Keychain items, databases, or logs.
> - iCloud sync of usage history, the local HTTP API, the log file, the Pi provider, and menu-bar stars.
>
> **If you script the `openusage` command:** the JSON changed. `providers` is keyed by account id (`codex@1a2b3c4d`), not by provider, and `schema` is now `openusage.limits.v2`.
>
> Background and discussion: [#1441](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/issues/1441)

detail.readme:
# OpenUsage Track your AI coding subscriptions from the macOS menu bar. OpenUsage shows how much of each AI plan you've used: session and weekly limits, credits, and balances, all in one panel. The limits closest to running out sit right in the menu bar. | | Light | Dark | | --- | --- | --- | | **Priority** | | | | **All Usage** | | | ## Installation - **Homebrew:** ```sh brew install --cask openusage ``` - **Direct download:** grab the latest universal DMG from the [releases page](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/releases/latest), open it, and drag OpenUsage to your Applications folder. The app updates itself with signed, notarized [Sparkle](docs/updates.md) updates. Requires macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel. ## Supported Providers - **[Claude](docs/providers.md#claude)**: session, weekly, model limits, extra usage (Enterprise spend), rate-limit resets - **[ChatGPT](docs/providers.md#chatgpt)**: session, weekly, Spark, extra usage, credit limit, rate-limit resets, daily tokens - **[Cursor](docs/providers.md#cursor)**: total usage, model usage, extra usage, requests, credits, daily spend and tokens - **[Amp](docs/providers.md#amp)**: agent usage, orb hours, Amp Free, credits - **[Antigravity](docs/providers.md#antigravity)**: Gemini, Argon, and Claude quotas - **[Copilot](docs/providers.md#copilot)**: credits, extra usage, chat, completions, organization billing, GitHub Enterprise on GHE.com - **[Devin](docs/providers.md#devin)**: daily and weekly quota, extra usage - **[Grok](docs/providers.md#grok)**: weekly limit, extra usage - **[Muse Code](docs/providers.md#muse-code)**: session, weekly - **[Ollama](docs/providers.md#ollama)**: session, weekly, monthly, extra usage, daily usage and tokens - **[OpenCode](docs/providers.md#opencode)**: session, weekly, monthly - **[OpenRouter](docs/providers.md#openrouter)**: balance, spend, key limit, budget - **[Z.ai](docs/providers.md#zai)**: session, weekly, web searches, rate-limit resets - **[CLIProxyAPI hubs](docs/cliproxyapi.md)**: every Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Devin, and Grok login on a [CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI) server Add your accounts from the app's Accounts screen. OpenUsage never reads other tools' credentials, files, or logs. See [Accounts](docs/accounts.md). Coming from 0.7.x? See [Upgrading from 0.7.x](docs/settings.md#upgrading-from-07x). ## Features - **Menu bar.** The limits closest to running out, at a glance. - **Priority.** What's running low, what's used up, and which accounts need you. - **All Usage.** Every account and limit in one place, with resets, your pace, and an optional mark where an even pace would be. - **Your layout.** Pin the metrics you care about, hide the rest with a right-click, and drag everything into your order. - **Unify multiple accounts.** Show your Claude or ChatGPT accounts as one card, with one bar per limit. - **Rate-limit resets.** See and spend Claude and ChatGPT resets. - **Share.** Copy a picture of your usage to the clipboard. - **Notifications.** A heads-up before a limit runs out, or before a weekly limit resets with most of it unused. - **Priority limits.** Choose how much left turns a limit orange or red, see limits you're burning through too fast while they still have plenty left, and see limits about to reset mostly unused. - **Global shortcut.** Toggle the panel from anywhere. - **[Command line](docs/cli.md).** Your usage as JSON, for scripts and agents. - **[Automatic updates](docs/updates.md).** Signed, notarized updates, with an optional beta channel. - **[Proxy support](docs/proxy.md).** Route provider requests through a SOCKS5, HTTP, or HTTPS proxy. ## Documentation How everything works, in [docs/](docs/README.md): - [Dashboard](docs/dashboard.md) - [Accounts](docs/accounts.md) and [CLIProxyAPI hubs](docs/cliproxyapi.md) - [Providers](docs/providers.md) - [Menu bar](docs/menu-bar.md) - [Settings](docs/settings.md) - [Refreshing](docs/refreshing.md) - [Command line](docs/cli.md) - [Updates](docs/updates.md) - [Proxy](docs/proxy.md) - [Privacy](docs/privacy.md), including optional daily provider account counts ## License [MIT](LICENSE) ---
Build from source ```sh swift build # debug build script/test_quiet.sh # run the tests without them taking the keyboard or the screen ./script/build_and_run.sh # build and launch the dev app from dist/ ``` `script/test_quiet.sh` takes `swift test` arguments such as `--filter`. The dev app has its own bundle identifier, so it runs beside an installed OpenUsage. See [debugging](docs/debugging.md). To learn the code, read the [architecture overview](docs/architecture.md), [adding a provider](docs/adding-a-provider.md), and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
Releasing Create the GitHub Release for the tag as a draft with its notes, then push a `v*` tag on `main` to build, sign, notarize, and publish it. A tag without a release that has notes fails before the build. - A plain tag (`v0.8.0`) ships to everyone. - A pre-release tag (`v0.8.0-beta.1`) ships to the beta channel. The pipeline is [release.yml](.github/workflows/release.yml), and the steps are in the `release-swift` skill. ### Release setup (one-time) The workflow needs these repository secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions): | Secret | What it is | | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE` | base64 of your Developer ID Application `.p12` | | `APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` | the password set when exporting that `.p12` | | `APPLE_ID` | the Apple ID email used for notarization | | `APPLE_PASSWORD` | an app-specific password for that Apple ID | | `APPLE_TEAM_ID` | your Apple Developer team ID | | `SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY` | base64 EdDSA public key, baked into the build as `SUPublicEDKey` | | `SPARKLE_PRIVATE_KEY` | base64 EdDSA private key used to sign the DMG | | `POSTHOG_CLI_API_KEY` | PostHog personal API key used to upload dSYMs for crash symbolication | | `POSTHOG_CLI_PROJECT_ID` | numeric PostHog project ID the dSYMs upload to | - Export the Developer ID Application certificate, with its private key, from Keychain Access as a `.p12`. Then run `base64 -i DeveloperID.p12 | pbcopy`. - Create the app-specific password at appleid.apple.com → Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords. - Generate the Sparkle key pair once with Sparkle's `generate_keys` tool. If the two keys don't match, signing is silently skipped. - The `POSTHOG_CLI_*` secrets only upload dSYMs so crash reports symbolicate. Without `POSTHOG_CLI_API_KEY`, the workflow skips the upload with a warning and the release still ships. The key comes from PostHog → Settings → Personal API keys, and the project ID is the number in your project URL. - Keep the repository public, because Sparkle fetches the DMG and appcast anonymously. After the first release, confirm that Settings → Pages → Source is GitHub Actions; `deploy-pages.yml` publishes `gh-pages`.
Contributing Pull requests are issue-first: 1. Comment on an issue. 2. Wait for a maintainer to add the `approved` label and assign it to you. 3. Open your PR with `Fixes #123`. Automation closes external PRs that skip this. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. Report security issues privately per [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). The OpenUsage name and logo are covered by the [trademark policy](TRADEMARK.md).
